questions.stem: In the SI system, electric current is measured in
questions.explanation: The ampere is the SI base unit of electric current. The volt measures potential difference, the ohm measures resistance and the coulomb measures charge, so they are different quantities. Remember the other base units too: metre, kilogram, second, kelvin, mole and candela.

optionRationale.1: The volt is the unit of potential difference.
optionRationale.3: The ohm is the unit of resistance.
optionRationale.4: The coulomb is the unit of electric charge.

questions.objective: Recall SI units of electrical quantities

questions.stem: Which cell organelle is the site of protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes read the instructions carried from the nucleus and join amino acids into proteins. They may lie free in the cytoplasm or be attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum. A quick way to remember is that proteins are made at ribosomes, while energy is released at mitochondria.

optionRationale.1: The mitochondrion releases energy from food.
optionRationale.2: Lysosomes digest waste material inside the cell.
optionRationale.3: The vacuole stores water and dissolved substances.

questions.objective: Recall organelle functions

questions.stem: The chemical symbol of sodium is
questions.explanation: The symbol Na comes from the Latin name natrium. Potassium is K, sulphur is S and tin is Sn, so these are symbols of other elements. Learn the symbols of common elements such as Na, K, Fe, Cu, Ag, Au, Pb and Hg for quick recall.

optionRationale.1: K is the symbol of potassium.
optionRationale.3: S is the symbol of sulphur.
optionRationale.4: Sn is the symbol of tin.

questions.objective: Recall symbols of elements

questions.stem: Which vitamin is made in the human skin when it is exposed to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Sunlight helps the skin to make vitamin D. Lack of it causes rickets in children, and the other vitamins listed are obtained mostly from food. Cod liver oil, egg yolk and fish are also dietary sources, and exposure to morning sunlight helps the body.

optionRationale.1: Vitamin A is obtained mainly from the diet.
optionRationale.2: Vitamin C is obtained from fruits and vegetables.
optionRationale.4: Vitamin K comes from the diet and from intestinal bacteria.

questions.objective: Recall the source of vitamin D

questions.stem: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
questions.explanation: Wind energy is replenished naturally and can be used again and again. Coal, petroleum and natural gas are fossil fuels formed over millions of years and will be exhausted one day. Natural resources that renew themselves quickly are called renewable, while the others are exhaustible.

optionRationale.1: Coal is a fossil fuel that will be exhausted.
optionRationale.2: Natural gas is a fossil fuel.
optionRationale.4: Petroleum is a fossil fuel that takes millions of years to form.

questions.objective: Distinguish renewable and non-renewable sources

questions.stem: Which gas forms the largest part, by volume, of the air we breathe?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78 per cent of dry air. Oxygen is about 21 per cent, argon about 1 per cent, and carbon dioxide is present only in traces. Argon is the third most common gas and carbon dioxide is only about 0.04 per cent of dry air.

optionRationale.1: Oxygen is about one fifth of the air.
optionRationale.2: Carbon dioxide is only a small fraction of a per cent.
optionRationale.3: Argon is present in a little less than one per cent.

questions.objective: Recall the composition of air

questions.stem: Blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart are called
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart to the organs and have thick, elastic walls. Veins bring blood back to the heart, and capillaries connect the two kinds of vessels. This is why veins and arteries differ in wall thickness and why only veins have valves.

optionRationale.1: Veins carry blood towards the heart.
optionRationale.3: Capillaries are thin vessels where exchange with the tissues happens.
optionRationale.4: Valves are flaps that prevent backflow and are not vessels.

questions.objective: Distinguish arteries and veins

questions.stem: Which of the following cannot travel through a vacuum?
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a material medium such as air, water or a solid. Light, radio waves and X-rays are electromagnetic waves, so they can pass through a vacuum. Sound needs a medium, and that is why astronauts on the Moon talk through radio.

optionRationale.1: Light is an electromagnetic wave and needs no medium.
optionRationale.3: Radio waves are electromagnetic waves.
optionRationale.4: X-rays are electromagnetic waves.

questions.objective: Recall which waves need a medium

questions.stem: Which of the following is non-biodegradable?
questions.explanation: Polythene is a synthetic plastic that microbes cannot break down, so it persists in the environment for hundreds of years. Peels, cotton cloth and vegetable waste are plant material that decays. Burning plastic also releases harmful gases, so it should be recycled or disposed of properly.

optionRationale.1: A banana peel is broken down by microbes.
optionRationale.2: Cotton is a natural fibre that decomposes.
optionRationale.4: Vegetable waste is decomposed by bacteria and fungi.

questions.objective: Classify wastes as biodegradable or not

questions.stem: The sour taste of vinegar is due to the presence of
questions.explanation: Vinegar is a solution of acetic acid in water, which gives it its sour taste. Citrus fruits contain citric acid, curd contains lactic acid and ant stings contain formic acid. Acetic acid is a weak organic acid, and a few per cent solution of it is sold as vinegar.

optionRationale.1: Citric acid is found in lemon and orange.
optionRationale.2: Lactic acid is present in sour milk and curd.
optionRationale.3: Formic acid is found in ant and nettle stings.

questions.objective: Recall natural acids

questions.stem: The SI unit of frequency is
questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of oscillations per second, and one hertz is one oscillation per second. The decibel measures loudness, the watt power and the pascal pressure. Heinrich Hertz gave his name to this unit, and one kilohertz equals one thousand oscillations per second.

optionRationale.2: The decibel is a unit of sound level.
optionRationale.3: The watt is the unit of power.
optionRationale.4: The pascal is the unit of pressure.

questions.objective: Recall SI units

questions.stem: A vehicle moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest with a uniform retardation of 5 m/s^2. The distance covered before it stops is
questions.explanation: Use v^2 = u^2 + 2as with v = 0, u = 20 and a = -5: 0 = 400 - 10s, so s = 40 m. The stopping time is 20 / 5 = 4 s, and the average speed of 10 m/s over 4 s also gives 40 m.

optionRationale.1: This is u squared divided by a, which leaves out the factor of 2.
optionRationale.3: This takes the speed as the distance.
optionRationale.4: This is the time taken to stop in seconds.

questions.objective: Apply the third equation of motion

questions.stem: A machine does 600 J of work in 20 s. Its power is
questions.explanation: Power is work divided by time: 600 J / 20 s = 30 W. One watt equals one joule per second, so in each second the machine does 30 J of work. A quick check is that the product of power and time in seconds gives back the work in joules.

optionRationale.1: This multiplies work by time instead of dividing.
optionRationale.2: This divides time by work, the inverse of the correct ratio.
optionRationale.4: This subtracts the time from the work.

questions.objective: Calculate power from work and time

questions.stem: Resistors of 2 ohm, 3 ohm and 5 ohm are connected in series across a 20 V battery. The potential difference across the 3 ohm resistor is
questions.explanation: In series the resistances add: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 ohm. The current is 20 / 10 = 2 A in every resistor. The voltage across the 3 ohm resistor is I x R = 2 x 3 = 6 V.

optionRationale.1: This is the total voltage; in series it is shared among the resistors.
optionRationale.2: This is the total resistance in ohms, not a voltage.
optionRationale.3: This is the current in amperes, not a voltage.

questions.objective: Find the voltage across one resistor in series

questions.stem: An atom has atomic number 17 and mass number 35. The number of neutrons in its nucleus is
questions.explanation: Mass number = protons + neutrons, and the atomic number gives the protons. So neutrons = 35 - 17 = 18. The number of electrons in the neutral atom equals the protons, 17. This also shows why isotopes of one element differ in mass number but not in atomic number.

optionRationale.2: This is the number of protons.
optionRationale.3: This is the mass number, which includes the protons.
optionRationale.4: This adds the atomic number and mass number.

questions.objective: Calculate neutrons from atomic and mass numbers

questions.stem: The pH of a 0.01 M solution of sodium hydroxide, a strong base, at 25 degrees Celsius is
questions.explanation: Sodium hydroxide ionises completely, so the hydroxide ion concentration is 10^-2 M and pOH = 2. At 25 degrees Celsius pH + pOH = 14, so pH = 12, which is basic. Always check whether the compound is an acid or a base before choosing between pH and pOH.

optionRationale.1: This would be the pH of 0.01 M strong acid.
optionRationale.3: This would need a base of concentration 0.0001 M.
optionRationale.4: This would need a base of concentration 0.1 M.

questions.objective: Calculate the pH of a strong base

questions.stem: Methane burns as CH4 + 2O2 gives CO2 + 2H2O. What mass of carbon dioxide forms when 8 g of methane burns completely? (Atomic masses: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation: The molar mass of methane is 16 g and that of CO2 is 44 g. One mole of CH4 gives one mole of CO2, so 8 g (half a mole) of methane gives half a mole, which is 22 g of carbon dioxide.

optionRationale.1: This is the mass formed from a full mole (16 g) of methane.
optionRationale.2: This is a quarter of a mole of CO2, not half.
optionRationale.4: This is the molar mass of methane, not the mass of the product.

questions.objective: Find the mass of a product from a balanced equation

questions.stem: Which component of blood mainly helps in clotting at the site of a cut?
questions.explanation: Platelets collect at an injury and, with clotting proteins in the plasma, form a clot that stops bleeding. Red cells carry oxygen and white cells fight infection. Remember that platelets are cell fragments formed in the bone marrow and have no nucleus.

optionRationale.1: Red blood cells carry oxygen.
optionRationale.2: White blood cells defend the body against germs.
optionRationale.3: Haemoglobin is the pigment that carries oxygen inside red cells.

questions.objective: Recall the function of blood platelets

questions.stem: Producers in an ecosystem store 50000 J of energy. By the ten per cent law, the energy available to the tertiary consumers is
questions.explanation: Primary consumers receive 10 per cent of 50000 J, which is 5000 J. Secondary consumers get 500 J, and tertiary consumers get 10 per cent of that, which is 50 J. Notice that each step multiplies the energy by 0.1, so three steps multiply it by 0.001.

optionRationale.2: This is the energy at the secondary consumer level.
optionRationale.3: This is the energy at the primary consumer level.
optionRationale.4: This is the energy at one more level, the fourth consumer.

questions.objective: Apply the ten per cent law over three levels

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about DDT in a food chain.
A. DDT is not broken down in the body, so it accumulates.
B. Its concentration is highest in the top carnivores.
C. Biomagnification means that the concentration decreases at higher trophic levels.
D. Producers carry the highest concentration of DDT.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: DDT is non-degradable and is not excreted, so it builds up in tissues and gets more concentrated at each higher level, reaching the maximum in top carnivores. This increase is biomagnification, so C and D are wrong.

optionRationale.1: C is wrong, because the concentration increases at higher levels.
optionRationale.3: D is wrong, because producers have the lowest concentration.
optionRationale.4: C and D are both wrong.

questions.objective: Explain biomagnification

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
Reason (R): Sound is a mechanical wave that needs a material medium for its propagation.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Sound travels by making the particles of a medium vibrate, so with no particles, as in a vacuum, it cannot travel. R correctly gives this reason, so both statements are true and R explains A.

optionRationale.2: R is the cause of A, so this option is wrong.
optionRationale.3: R is true, so this option is wrong.
optionRationale.4: A is true, so this option is wrong.

questions.objective: Relate sound propagation to a medium

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Aluminium is a good conductor of electricity.
Reason (R): Aluminium is a non-metal.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Aluminium is a metal, and metals have free electrons that conduct electricity well, so A is true. R is false because aluminium is a metal, not a non-metal, and non-metals are generally poor conductors.

optionRationale.1: R is false, so options 1 and 2 are wrong.
optionRationale.2: R is false, so options 1 and 2 are wrong.
optionRationale.4: A is true, so this option is wrong.

questions.objective: Link electrical conduction with metals

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements.
A. Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts.
B. Respiration releases energy from food.
C. Stomata allow the exchange of gases in leaves.
D. Mitochondria are the site of photosynthesis.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis, respiration releases the energy stored in food, and stomata let gases enter and leave leaves. Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration, so D is wrong. Remember also that the oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from the splitting of water.

optionRationale.2: B and C are also correct, and D is wrong.
optionRationale.3: D is wrong, because mitochondria are the site of respiration.
optionRationale.4: D is wrong, so not all four are correct.

questions.objective: Distinguish photosynthesis and respiration

questions.stem: Match List-I (disease) with List-II (type of causative organism).
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium (I). Dengue is caused by a virus (II). Tuberculosis is caused by a bacterium (III), and ringworm is a fungal skin infection (IV). Such matching items are common, so prepare a small table of diseases, causes and vectors.

optionRationale.1: It swaps the causes of malaria and dengue.
optionRationale.2: It swaps the causes of tuberculosis and ringworm.
optionRationale.4: Each pair is wrong.

questions.objective: Match diseases with the type of pathogen

questions.stem: Eutrophication of a pond is mainly caused by an excess of
questions.explanation: Nitrates and phosphates that run off from fields or come with sewage feed algae and cause blooms. When the algae die, bacteria use up the dissolved oxygen, which harms fish and other water life.

optionRationale.1: Carbon monoxide is an air pollutant and does not feed algae.
optionRationale.2: CFCs damage the ozone layer.
optionRationale.3: Sulphur dioxide leads to acid rain.

questions.objective: Identify the cause of eutrophication

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of ex situ conservation?
questions.explanation: Ex situ conservation protects species outside their natural habitat, as in zoos, botanical gardens and seed banks. National parks, sanctuaries and biosphere reserves are in situ methods. Gene banks and seed banks are also ex situ methods, since they preserve genetic material outside the wild.

optionRationale.1: A national park protects species in their natural habitat.
optionRationale.2: A sanctuary protects animals in their natural habitat.
optionRationale.3: A biosphere reserve protects ecosystems in their natural habitat.

questions.objective: Distinguish in situ and ex situ conservation

questions.stem: A convex mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles because it
options: gives an erect, smaller image and a wider field of view
forms a real, enlarged image of the traffic behind
converges the light from vehicles to a bright point
forms an inverted image that is easier to judge
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms an erect, virtual and diminished image. Because the image is smaller, the mirror shows a larger area behind the vehicle, which gives the driver a wider field of view.

optionRationale.2: A convex mirror never forms a real image of a real object.
optionRationale.3: A convex mirror diverges light rays.
optionRationale.4: The image in a convex mirror is erect.

questions.objective: Explain the use of a convex mirror

questions.stem: A block of mass 2.4 kg occupies a volume of 0.003 m^3. Its density is
questions.explanation: Density = mass / volume = 2.4 / 0.003 = 800 kg/m^3. This is less than the density of water, which is 1000 kg/m^3, so the block would float in water. Such a body floats in water because its density is less than that of water.

optionRationale.1: This is out by a factor of 10.
optionRationale.3: This is out by a factor of 10 the other way.
optionRationale.4: This divides the volume by the mass, the inverse ratio.

questions.objective: Calculate density

questions.stem: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a speed of 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s^2 and ignoring air resistance, the maximum height it reaches is
questions.explanation: At the top the speed is zero, so 0 = u^2 - 2gh, giving h = u^2 / 2g = 400 / 20 = 20 m. The time taken to reach the top is u / g = 2 s. Do not mix up the time to reach the top and the maximum height, which are different quantities.

optionRationale.1: This is u squared divided by g, which leaves out the factor of 2.
optionRationale.2: This is half the correct height.
optionRationale.4: This is the time to reach the top in seconds.

questions.objective: Find the maximum height of a body thrown upwards

questions.stem: A gas occupies 2 L at a pressure of 1 atm. At constant temperature its volume is reduced to 0.5 L. Its new pressure is
questions.explanation: By Boyle's law, P1 V1 = P2 V2 at constant temperature. So P2 = 1 x 2 / 0.5 = 4 atm. The volume falls to one quarter, so the pressure rises four times. The relation holds only when the temperature and the amount of gas stay constant.

optionRationale.1: This inverts the ratio of the volumes.
optionRationale.2: This halves the volume instead of reducing it to a quarter.
optionRationale.3: This is the new volume, not a pressure.

questions.objective: Apply Boyle's law

questions.stem: Hydrogen burns in oxygen as 2H2 + O2 gives 2H2O. What mass of water is formed when 4 g of hydrogen burns completely? (Atomic masses: H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation: The molar mass of H2 is 2 g, so 4 g is 2 mol. The equation shows 2 mol of H2 give 2 mol of water, and water has molar mass 18 g, so 36 g forms. It uses 32 g of oxygen, and 4 + 32 = 36.

optionRationale.2: This is the mass of one mole of water, but 4 g of H2 is two moles.
optionRationale.3: This is the mass of oxygen needed, not of water formed.
optionRationale.4: This doubles the correct mass.

questions.objective: Calculate the mass of water formed in a reaction

questions.stem: An iron nail dipped in copper sulphate solution becomes covered with a reddish-brown deposit. This happens because iron
options: is less reactive than copper and is displaced by it
is more reactive than copper and displaces it from the solution
reacts with the water of the solution to form copper
acts only as a catalyst without taking part in the reaction
questions.explanation: Iron lies above copper in the reactivity series, so it takes the place of copper in copper sulphate. Copper metal gets deposited on the nail, and the blue colour of the solution fades to pale green as iron sulphate forms.

optionRationale.1: Then copper would not be deposited on the iron nail.
optionRationale.3: Copper cannot be formed from water, which has no copper.
optionRationale.4: Iron itself goes into the solution as ions.

questions.objective: Explain a displacement reaction

questions.stem: Two 60 W bulbs are used for 10 hours and a 1000 W heater for 2 hours. The total electrical energy consumed is
questions.explanation: The bulbs use 2 x 60 W x 10 h = 1200 Wh = 1.2 kWh. The heater uses 1000 W x 2 h = 2000 Wh = 2.0 kWh. The total is 1.2 + 2.0 = 3.2 kWh, that is, 3.2 units of electricity.

optionRationale.1: This counts the heater only.
optionRationale.2: This counts the two bulbs only.
optionRationale.4: This counts only one bulb along with the heater.

questions.objective: Calculate energy consumption in kilowatt hours

questions.stem: A force of 20 N acts on a 5 kg body, initially at rest, for 3 s on a smooth surface. The kinetic energy of the body at the end of 3 s is
questions.explanation: The acceleration is a = F / m = 20 / 5 = 4 m/s^2, so after 3 s the speed is v = 12 m/s. The kinetic energy is (1/2) m v^2 = 0.5 x 5 x 144 = 360 J.

optionRationale.1: This leaves out the factor of one half.
optionRationale.2: This is only the square of the speed, not multiplied by half the mass.
optionRationale.3: This is the product of force and time, which is the impulse and not energy.

questions.objective: Combine Newton's second law and kinetic energy

questions.stem: A 2 kg body moving at 6 m/s collides with a 4 kg body at rest and the two stick together. The speed of the combined body just after the collision is
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved: 2 x 6 + 4 x 0 = 12 kg m/s before. After the collision the combined mass is 6 kg, so the speed is 12 / 6 = 2 m/s. Some kinetic energy is lost, because the collision is inelastic.

optionRationale.2: This is the average of 6 and 0 m/s, which ignores the masses.
optionRationale.3: This ignores the increased mass of the system.
optionRationale.4: This divides the momentum by 3 instead of by 6 kg.

questions.objective: Apply conservation of momentum

questions.stem: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. The image formed is
options: virtual, erect and enlarged, behind the mirror
real, inverted and of the same size, at 30 cm from the mirror
real, inverted and diminished, between F and C
real, inverted and magnified, beyond C
questions.explanation: The radius of curvature is 2 x 15 = 30 cm, so the object is at the centre of curvature. With the mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f and u = -30, f = -15, we get v = -30 cm. The image is real, inverted and the same size.

optionRationale.1: This happens only when the object is closer than the focus.
optionRationale.3: This happens only when the object is beyond the centre of curvature.
optionRationale.4: This happens only when the object is between F and C.

questions.objective: Locate an image formed by a concave mirror

questions.stem: A solution has pH 3. It is diluted to 100 times its volume with water. Its pH becomes about
questions.explanation: The hydrogen ion concentration is 10^-3 M at pH 3. A 100-fold dilution makes it 10^-5 M, so pH = 5. The solution is still acidic, since water cannot raise the pH above 7 in this way.

optionRationale.1: This would be the pH after a dilution of 10 times.
optionRationale.2: This is a move in the wrong direction, towards a stronger acid.
optionRationale.4: Diluting an acid with water cannot make it exactly neutral.

questions.objective: Estimate the pH after dilution

questions.stem: Two tall pea plants, both of genotype Tt, are crossed. Out of 400 offspring, how many are expected to be short (tt)?
questions.explanation: A Tt x Tt cross gives TT, Tt, Tt and tt in the ratio 1:2:1, so 3/4 are tall and 1/4 are short. One quarter of 400 is 100 short plants, a 3:1 tall to short ratio.

optionRationale.1: This is the expected number of tall plants.
optionRationale.2: This assumes half of the offspring are short.
optionRationale.3: This is one third of the offspring.

questions.objective: Apply Mendel's monohybrid ratio

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): A person with blood group AB can receive red blood cells of any ABO group.
Reason (R): The plasma of group AB blood contains neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Because AB plasma has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies, donor red cells of A, B, AB or O do not get attacked, so AB persons are universal recipients for the ABO system. R is the reason for A.

optionRationale.2: R directly explains A, so option 2 is wrong.
optionRationale.3: R is true, so this option is wrong.
optionRationale.4: A is true, so this option is wrong.

questions.objective: Relate blood group AB to its antibodies

questions.stem: Match List-I (hormone) with List-II (gland that secretes it).
questions.explanation: Insulin comes from the pancreas (I), thyroxine from the thyroid (II), adrenaline from the adrenal glands (III) and growth hormone from the pituitary gland (IV). Hence A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV. Glands and their secretions are standard NCERT facts, so revise them as a table.

optionRationale.1: It swaps the glands for insulin and thyroxine.
optionRationale.3: It swaps the glands for adrenaline and growth hormone.
optionRationale.4: Every pair is wrong.

questions.objective: Match hormones with their glands

questions.stem: In the food chain grass, grasshopper, frog, snake, eagle, the grass stores 100000 J of energy. By the ten per cent law, the energy reaching the eagle is
questions.explanation: The energy falls to a tenth at each of the four transfers: 100000 gives 10000 J (grasshopper), 1000 J (frog), 100 J (snake) and 10 J (eagle). Thus 100000 x (0.1)^4 = 10 J.

optionRationale.1: This is the energy at the snake, one level before the eagle.
optionRationale.2: This takes one more transfer than the chain has.
optionRationale.4: This is the energy at the frog, two levels earlier.

questions.objective: Apply the ten per cent law along a food chain

questions.stem: Match List-I (international agreement) with List-II (main concern).
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol deals with ozone-depleting substances (I), the Ramsar Convention with wetlands (II), CITES with international trade in endangered species (III), and the Kyoto Protocol with limiting greenhouse gas emissions (IV). Learn each agreement together with its main concern, since questions usually test this pairing.

optionRationale.2: It swaps the concerns of the Montreal and Kyoto protocols.
optionRationale.3: It swaps the concerns of the Ramsar Convention and CITES.
optionRationale.4: Every pair is wrong.

questions.objective: Match international agreements with their subjects

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements.
A. Biogas consists mainly of methane.
B. Biodegradable kitchen waste can be turned into compost.
C. Glass and plastic are biodegradable materials.
D. Wind and solar energy are renewable.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Biogas from cattle dung and plant waste is mostly methane. Kitchen waste decomposes into compost, and wind and solar energy are renewable. Glass and plastic are non-biodegradable, which is why recycling matters, so C is wrong.

optionRationale.2: B and D are also correct, and C is wrong.
optionRationale.3: C is wrong, as glass and plastic do not decompose naturally.
optionRationale.4: C is wrong, so not all four are correct.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on waste and energy

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Depletion of the ozone layer is the main cause of global warming.
Reason (R): The ozone layer absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: A is false because global warming is caused mainly by greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane, while ozone depletion lets more ultraviolet reach the Earth. R is true, since the ozone layer absorbs ultraviolet radiation.

optionRationale.1: A is false, so options 1, 2 and 3 are wrong.
optionRationale.2: A is false, so options 1, 2 and 3 are wrong.
optionRationale.3: R is true, so this option is wrong.

questions.objective: Separate ozone depletion from global warming

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Without the natural greenhouse effect, the average surface temperature of the Earth would be far lower.
Reason (R): Greenhouse gases trap part of the heat radiated by the Earth's surface.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Gases such as carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour hold back part of the outgoing heat and so keep the surface warm enough for life. R explains why the greenhouse effect warms the planet, so it is the correct reason for A.

optionRationale.2: R is the right explanation of A, so this option is wrong.
optionRationale.3: R is true, so this option is wrong.
optionRationale.4: A is true, so this option is wrong.

questions.objective: Explain the natural greenhouse effect
